workbookName: Batch 1 Part A - Script-Tier Tag Set (Circuit Breakers, Amber Brown)

rows.synopsis: Starting middle school without her best friend, Justin, makes Amber all the more grateful for new friend and neighbor Brandi.
rows.situation: starting middle school without your best friend; parents' divorce doing its everyday work (dad abroad, mom's new boyfriend); a new friend next door
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (middle school without Justin, grateful for Brandi); Amber's video diary is the device that models naming feelings (I, Amber Brown, do not like change); new friendship eases the transition

rows.synopsis: Amber and Brandi find a diamond ring, which leads Amber to believe her mom is about to do something Amber's not quite ready for.
rows.situation: worry that mom is about to remarry before dad comes home; mixed-up loyalties between two parents; wanting to be included by the popular crowd
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (found diamond ring, not ready for mom's news); names the real question out loud, how do you decide whose happiness is most important; the fortune-cookie dinner talk lands her in an honest moment with mom; topics: none defensible (family story (mom's remarriage worry) - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: Amber sets aside her fears and auditions for the school play, while her dad moves into a new apartment.
rows.situation: living between two homes after divorce (first sleepover at dad's new apartment); setting aside fear to audition for the school play
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (auditions for the play, dad moves into a new apartment); Brandi's friendship gives her the courage to audition (asking for help); parents' first civil custody talk is the adult-side resolution

rows.synopsis: It's the night of the play and Amber's nervous. She hopes her dad, who's stuck in traffic, makes it in time to see her debut.
rows.situation: not getting the part you dreamed of (Angry Apple Tree Number 3, not Dorothy); embarrassment about a small role; performing anyway on play night
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (play night, nervous, dad stuck in traffic); mom and Justin reframe the small role (you took a risk, be proud you branched out); she nearly quits, then performs

rows.synopsis: Amber wants to get her ears pierced, just like Brandi, so she enlists the help of Aunt Pam to try persuading her mom.
rows.situation: wanting to grow up faster than the rules allow (pierced ears before 13); feeling controlled by the grown-ups' minute-by-minute schedule; first-school-dance worries
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (ears pierced via Aunt Pam to persuade mom); the kid-side conflict stays open at episode's end (she decides to stop listening); the resolution modeled is the adults' talk about boundaries as love, flagged for the batch review; topics: none defensible (body/rules story (ear piercing) - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: As the girls get ready for their first school dance, Amber feels bad about disobeying her mom and wants to come clean.
rows.situation: doing something against a clear rule in secret (ear piercing); guilt versus wanting to keep the secret; repairing trust with mom
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (feels bad about disobeying mom and wants to come clean); confession costs her the dance; mom names the real stake, we do not lie to each other, that is what makes us us

rows.synopsis: When Amber's new math tutor turns out to be an old crush of her dad's, she and Brandi form a plan so that she'll never need a tutor again.
rows.situation: divorce adjustment: sharing a newly returned dad and worrying about being loved less when he might date again; the sadness that comes in waves
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (math tutor is dad's old crush, plan to not need a tutor); mom's honest comfort carries the resolution (it is still love, just changed its shape; sad times come in waves too); the tutor scheme is mischievous, not mean

rows.synopsis: Amber's house is overrun by a film crew, which has the surprising effect of bringing the family together, much to Amber's delight.
rows.situation: a film crew overruns the house; stage fright on camera (mom freezes, Pam fills in); wanting your blended family to have one good day together
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (house overrun by film crew, family pulled together); Sarah hands her segment to Pam when panic hits, and the family covers for each other; Amber's real pride beat is her B-plus in math; topics: none defensible (filmmaking story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: While volunteering at a nursing home, Amber befriends a resident and bends the facility's rules in the spirit of love and friendship.
rows.situation: an unexpected intergenerational friendship (a lonely nursing-home resident); volunteering; bending facility rules out of love; a parent hiding that he feels unwell
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (nursing home volunteering, befriends a resident, bends the rules); listening is the literal resolution (what older people want most is someone who will listen); content consideration: the kids quietly take Cecile off-site, modeled as loving but against the rules, flagged for batch review; topics: none defensible (nursing-home friendship story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: The family rallies together to sneak Cecile back into the nursing home, but the fun is interrupted by unexpected news.
rows.situation: a parent's sudden heart surgery; family rallying (dad moving in to recover while mom is engaged to Max); giving a lonely elder a place in the friend group
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (sneaking Cecile back, interrupted by unexpected news); the news is dad's bypass surgery and the family rallies, you can always call us; the friend oath closes it; content consideration: the surgery scare, played warm not frightening; topics: none defensible (nursing-home/family-health story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: Jacob is desperate to make the school track team and his height is holding him back. Can a medical research lab help him grow faster?
rows.situation: being different (a short kid's height holds him back from the track team); a risky shortcut to change your body
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Jacob, track tryouts, medibots); resolution models self-acceptance, Jacob lands on being happy with who he was; medibot side effects are a mild sci-fi scare element

rows.synopsis: Aspiring dancer Jesse can't balance his priorities, so a friend builds his robotic duplicate. But things take a turn when Jesse loses control of his double.
rows.situation: nervous about performing (dance team audition); tempted to cheat instead of doing it yourself; an overpacked schedule
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Jesse, dance audition, helper robot); Jesse declines to cheat at the audition and apologizes to Cara for misusing her science project; he loses the spot but keeps his integrity

rows.synopsis: After her parents' divorce, Emily uses a memory therapy device to relive happier times, until an error threatens to erase the past forever.
rows.situation: parents' separation and divorce; scheming to reunite them; a mistake that is hard to admit
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Emily, memory therapy device, divorce); resolution is the parents' honest talk (not getting back together, still a family) plus Emily confessing what she did; synopsis field restructures the catalog em dash per the dash-free house rule; topics: none defensible (divorce/memory-device story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: Carefree student Seth and his strict principal mistakenly swap bodies when a school presentation goes wrong.
rows.situation: walking in someone else's shoes (a student swaps bodies with the principal); honesty about who stole the test answers
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Seth, Principal Young body swap); Logan's guilt over the stolen test key and Seth choosing not to let her take the fall carry the honesty beat; principal learns student life is hard, student learns the principal's job is hard

rows.synopsis: When time seemingly freezes, a mismatched group of students get trapped in detention and must work together to find a way out.
rows.situation: mismatched students trapped in a frozen-time detention, forced to work together; fear that your best effort is never good enough
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (detention, time freeze, Mr. Hodge experiment); Yasmine and Madison trade apologies about grades and effort; Ben's memorized handbook and Madison's remembered science save the day, teamwork is the engine of the resolution

rows.synopsis: Siblings Jack and Cassady buy a new remote for their media room and discover it can control their overbearing parents, for better and worse.
rows.situation: parents' rules that feel babyish (parental controls); a scary game behind their backs; a nightmare that shows what comfort you actually need
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Jack and Cassady, the remote, parental controls); after the nightmare Jack admits the game scared him and asks for the controls back, and the kids confess the whole scheme; parents apologize for going overboard; topics: none defensible (tech-gadget story (parents controlled by a remote) - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: In a self-sustaining home on Mars, Cricket and her family prepare to host visitors, but a storm jeopardizes their plans and safety.
rows.situation: living far from home (a family isolated on Mars); a canceled visit with your only in-person friend; a storm that tests family teamwork
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Cricket, Mars habitat, storm); Cricket names feeling everything at once after the simulation reveal, and the family's honest talks carry the resolution; mild peril (oxygen leak) is procedural, not scary

rows.synopsis: After striking a deal with his mom and dad, Josh starts his public school journey, but a mishap makes it hard to blend in.
rows.situation: starting public school after years of homeschooling; deciding when to share a visible difference (a prosthetic leg); an embarrassing first-day moment in front of everyone
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (public school deal, mishap makes blending in hard); the day ends in a dad talk, why do we fall, so we can learn to pick ourselves back up; Josh hides the fall from mom, flagged as a thread the next episode resolves

rows.synopsis: Principal Keifer offers access to a school resource. Meanwhile, Josh attempts to shake a nickname and Kyle makes a plan to boost their popularity.
rows.situation: unwanted special treatment (an elevator key that makes you stand out); wanting to be seen without being labeled; coming clean to mom about a school incident days late
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Keifer offers the resource, Josh shakes the nickname, Kyle's popularity plan); Josh insists on the same discipline as any student and asks mom to hold him accountable; Kyle's invisible-kid thread tagged on the situation side

rows.synopsis: Josh enthusiastically joins every club but learns there are only so many hours in a day, and he quickly falls short as a friend to Gabriella.
rows.situation: overcommitting (joining every club) and letting a friend down; fear of missing out colliding with only so many hours in a day
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (every club, falls short as a friend to Gabriella); Josh misses B&B until he is killed off in the campaign, then apologizes by showing back up; mom's roller-coaster advice, pick one and enjoy it, carries the reframe

rows.synopsis: A surprise at soccer tryouts challenges Josh's confidence and ruffles the feathers of a fellow teammate.
rows.situation: doubting whether you earned your spot (did mom's involvement get it for me?); wanting to succeed or fail on your own without parents clearing the way
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (tryouts surprise, ruffled teammate); Josh asks mom directly, gets an honest answer, and accepts being benched as proof the starting spot was earned; tagged toward 8-10 for the fairness-of-effort theme

rows.synopsis: After making mistakes on a math quiz, Josh questions his abilities and struggles to share his feelings with Kyle and Gabriella.
rows.situation: bombing a surprise quiz and spiraling into all-or-nothing thinking; taking the stress out on friends; wanting to retreat to what is comfortable (back to homeschool)
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (quiz mistakes, struggles to share feelings with Kyle and Gabriella); Josh apologizes to both friends and the green-gummy-bear truce lands; Luisa's tree-fort runaway is the comic mirror of wanting to run from a bad day

rows.synopsis: As the gang prepares for a costume showcase, Josh embraces an initially uncomfortable alteration, and Gabriella faces peer pressure.
rows.situation: a prosthetic leg breaking on the day you wanted to feel like every other kid; peer pressure to match the group's look; hiding versus showing up anyway
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (uncomfortable alteration embraced, Gabriella's peer pressure); dad's mirror talk, you get to decide whether different is good or bad, I see a butterfly, is the resolution beat; content consideration: none beyond the broken-device upset, played gently; topics: none defensible (Halloween costume story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: In hopes of having an epic movie night, Josh attempts to sneak a special treat into the theater, but a security guard throws a wrench in the plan.
rows.situation: a first outing without parents; a rule-breaking plan (sneaking drinks in) that backfires in front of everyone; wanting to prove you are grown up
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (sneaking a treat into the theater, security guard throws a wrench); the spray accident is owned and cleaned up and the night is salvaged at home with grandparents; content consideration: kids sneak sodas against theater rules, resolved with accountability; topics: none defensible (movie-theater outing story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: Josh meets Matt's skate park friends and takes his new prosthesis for a spin. Matt struggles with sharing the spotlight. Gabriella fields tough news.
rows.situation: a sibling feeling left out when one kid needs more attention (Josh's new leg day); losing the team captaincy you have held forever; sharing the spotlight with a friend
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (new prosthesis spin, Matt and the spotlight, Gabriella's tough news); the family meeting names it, some kids need more attention and our job is that no one feels less-than; Luisa faking Dr Squirrels' injury is the honest mirror

rows.synopsis: During a day of play, Josh has a hard time compromising with classmates when they realize he could offer them a competitive edge.
rows.situation: friends using your difference as a contest advantage; saying no to people who call you a legend; the line between generosity and being taken for granted
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (hard time compromising, competitive edge); dad's sundae talk, never too late to change your mind about what makes you comfortable, that's your leg not theirs, carries the resolution; Josh reclaims the relay

rows.synopsis: Josh attempts to make his first dance magical and meaningful. At home, his parents revisit a video of their first dance.
rows.situation: putting too much pressure on a big night to be perfect; a friend quietly carrying something heavy; the first school dance as a rite of passage
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (first dance made magical and meaningful, parents revisit their first-dance video); Josh names the real weight out loud, he lost his leg to cancer and is not officially cancer free for five years, so every first might also be a last; Gabriella admits she quit volleyball under pressure; content consideration: cancer backstory, handled warmly and factually

rows.synopsis: A clean bill of health means a new beginning for Ella, but going back to school tests her can-do spirit.
rows.situation: returning to school after a long illness (cancer treatment); being the kid everyone pities and asks about; a body that feels unpredictable; a best friend who stayed away when it counted
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (clean bill of health, new beginning, back to school tests her can-do spirit); Ella names her paper-towel trigger and tells her dad she is not ready but will not let that stop her; content considerations: cancer recovery, vomiting, pity from classmates, a friend's relapse (Gavin); sibling jealousy subplot (Grady)

rows.synopsis: As Ella encourages Kai to live in the moment, she attempts to let go of her past with Ximena. Grady discovers a new passion.
rows.situation: mending a friendship that broke during your illness; forgiving a friend who stayed away; living one day at a time when the future is scary
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Kai lives in the moment via ice-blocking, Ella lets go of her past with Ximena, Grady discovers soccer); the Kai conversation names her truth, she can only live one today at a time; content consideration: friend Gavin's cancer relapse

rows.synopsis: Ella searches for swimwear after being invited to a pool party. Grady makes a plan to step out of Ella's shadow at school.
rows.situation: feeling self-conscious about scars (surgery scars at a pool party); wanting to be seen as more than your illness; a sibling stepping out of the patient's shadow
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (swimwear search, pool party, Grady steps out of Ella's shadow); mom's bench talk flips the suit spiral into the cannonball; content consideration: mom hides the cancer from coworkers, which hurts Ella when discovered

rows.synopsis: A flashback offers a glimpse into Ella's interests, and anxieties, before everything changed. Grady and his dad search for a new shared hobby.
rows.situation: being pushed to join a club that is not you; a parent's picture of you versus who you are; finding the one person who will actually listen
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (flashback to before cancer, her interests and anxieties, Grady and dad seek a new hobby); the Pin Ceremony speech is the resolution, she says the true thing she practiced with Kai; content consideration: crying alone, pressure to conform; flashback structure; topics: none defensible (identity/club-pressure story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: The McCaffreys embark on a spontaneous camping trip. Ximena and Kai put their friendship to the test at an escape room.
rows.situation: a family stretched thin after a hard year (a parent who pretended, a sibling acting out, the silent treatment); a trip taken to force a reset; two friends learning to be friends without you
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (spontaneous camping trip, Ximena and Kai's escape-room test); every arc resolves in honest conversations on the roadside; content consideration: none beyond family conflict, played for comedy and warmth

rows.synopsis: Ella gets the chance to meet her favorite pop star and tries to make the most of the opportunity.
rows.situation: getting your wish when a friend in the hospital cannot have theirs; survivor's guilt; everyone celebrating you when you just want to be normal
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (meets favorite pop star Hayley Kiyoko, makes the most of it); Ella tells Hayley why she almost skipped the wish and turns it into a rooftop concert for the ward; Nurse Steve names survivor's guilt; content considerations: hospital treatment, neutropenic isolation, friend's relapse

rows.synopsis: At her first post-treatment sleepover, Ella navigates excitement and nerves. Grady enjoys being an only child for the night.
rows.situation: the first normal milestone after treatment (a sleepover); wanting one night without being the kid with a medical history; questions about the future that hurt
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (first post-treatment sleepover, excitement and nerves, Grady's only-child night); the sky lantern resolves it, she lets go of cancer and also wishes to never let it go; content consideration: a fertility-and-future question (the MASH game) lands hard; parents' forced attention subplot; topics: none defensible (sleepover milestone story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: Kai plans a series of exhilarating adventures, but Ella suspects he's hiding his true intentions. Grady takes up a new sport to impress friends.
rows.situation: hiding a secret from your best friend (family pressure, secretly quitting an activity); pretending to be someone you are not to fit in; academic pressure that feels like drowning
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Kai plans exhilarating adventures, Ella suspects he is hiding his true intentions, Grady takes up a sport to impress friends); Kai finally says he has never told anyone about the med-school pressure; content consideration: intense family achievement pressure, lying to friends, both resolved honestly

rows.synopsis: The origins of Ella's “live each moment to the fullest” attitude come to light.
rows.situation: being the only one your age in a hard place (a teen in a children's cancer ward); loneliness when nobody shares your experience; choosing your outlook when you cannot choose your room
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (the origins of Ella's live-each-moment attitude come to light, hospital flashbacks); the prison-or-palace reframe, naming the cancer Gina to separate it from yourself, then passing it on to Gavin; content considerations: pediatric cancer ward, chemo, mortality talk (mayfly speech), heavier than most of the series; topics: none defensible (hospital back story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: Pressure builds as Ella preps for a big day. Kai struggles to share his secret. Nurse Steve encourages Grady to face his feelings.
rows.situation: scan day, waiting to find out if the cancer is back; a friend's secret and family pressure building; feeling selfish for fearing for yourself when someone else is sick
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (pressure builds as Ella preps for a big day, Kai struggles to share his secret, Nurse Steve encourages Grady to face his feelings); Ella names scanxiety and admits she was scared for herself; the scan result stays open on purpose, the resolution is emotional honesty, not the medical outcome; content consideration: scan-day dread, possible relapse, unresolved at episode end; topics: none defensible (scan-day waiting story - no ratified topic fits)

rows.synopsis: Budding pop star Jasmine crafts a music video, and major surprise, with her friends.
rows.situation: wanting a future different from the one assigned to you; hiding a passion because the rules and parents forbid it; friends who share a forbidden dream
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (music video plus surprise, crashing the DMBEETZ concert); the band's own song, you have the right to choose, is the stand; the disguised-identity workaround is a series-long thread, not resolved here

rows.synopsis: The band makes a unique practice space their own. Meanwhile, their message of self-expression inspires a baker to break from the mold.
rows.situation: creative block when a song will not come; fear of being caught doing what you love; helping someone else break from their mold
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (unique practice space, baker breaks from the mold); Jasmine keeps working the chorus until free to be me lands; the crowd rallies for the baker when Goldenshorts threatens her new flavors

rows.synopsis: Jasmine discovers her math teacher longs to be a pro wrestler. To support her, the newly named Brushstrokes host an epic live event.
rows.situation: keeping a big secret from your parents and how much it weighs; helping an adult reach a hidden dream; discovering you can love your own role differently
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (math teacher longs to wrestle, band hosts the live event); Jasmine comes clean and finds her parents were once a musical duo who understand; Miss Milton stays a teacher but makes math her own; fair grounding accepted
rows.topics: Music & dance; School & books; Sports & games

rows.synopsis: DMBEETZ score a hit after stealing the Brushstrokes' song. Nick's mom shares her dream and asks for help stepping into the spotlight.
rows.situation: someone stealing your work and twisting its meaning; a parent who gave up their own dream; refusing to quit when the system is rigged
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (DMBEETZ score a hit after stealing the song, Nick's mom steps into the spotlight); Ms Hazard dances her own routine, this was never about winning; the band refuses to quit after the stolen song zombifies

rows.synopsis: Todd promises to get the Brushstrokes on BRBX Media, but their broadcast is threatened by Klaus' mischievous parents.
rows.situation: giving someone a second chance despite your doubts; accidentally helping the wrong people when trying to be agreeable; wanting not to become what your family is
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Todd promises the broadcast, Klaus's mischievous parents threaten it); friends reassure Klaus that trying to help and things going wrong is an everyone thing, not a you thing; content consideration: comic villainy (robot piranhas, window-breaking plan), all resolved

rows.synopsis: The Brushstrokes discover a rising star as they try to rewrite Ms. Goldenshorts' school musical.
rows.situation: an anxious understudy told she is never good enough to be a lead; stepping into the spotlight despite stage fright; a friend learning not to push someone else's moment
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (rising star discovered while rewriting the musical); Vanessa almost walks, Jasmine tells her confidence is her own to find, then she returns and sings the finale; content consideration: anxiety about performing, mean-girl undermining, resolved

rows.synopsis: A vengeful Ms. Goldenshorts goes all out to unmask the Brushstrokes. Jasmine recruits extra help to keep their secret safe.
rows.situation: group punishment for something you did not cause; pressure to snitch on friends; finding a way out that protects everyone
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Goldenshorts goes all out to unmask the band, Jasmine recruits help to keep the secret); Holly's third option is collective action, no one rats and everyone declares together; Jasmine and Ada both apologize for doubting Holly

rows.synopsis: While the Brushstrokes look for inspiration, Jasmine struggles to connect with a bandmate. Holly's family makes a deal with Ms. Goldenshorts.
rows.situation: a fight with your best friend that you caused; showing someone they matter without pretending; parents who smother out of worry; creating under deadline pressure
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Jasmine struggles to connect with a bandmate, Holly's family makes a deal with Goldenshorts); Jasmine admits the plan and tells Holly the truth about her over-wordy song, and Holly thanks her for not giving special treatment; Holly asks her parents for space to choose

rows.synopsis: A major opportunity at BRBX Media fuels anxiety. Jasmine tries to soothe her bandmates, but trouble awaits at the studio.
rows.situation: performance anxiety before the biggest moment of your life; discovering a friend's betrayal at the worst time; stage fright that spirals
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (major opportunity fuels anxiety, Jasmine soothes bandmates, trouble awaits at the studio); the band's calm-breathing, art-therapy and dance-therapy sequences, plus the heart of it, whatever happens we still have each other; content consideration: Todd's betrayal revealed, escape ends on the breakup-announcement cliff

rows.synopsis: The Brushstrokes plan a rooftop concert to prove they're still together...but things don't go as expected.
rows.situation: winning fans back after a public setback; letting a friend help again without fully forgetting the hurt; trusting a friend's plan you do not understand
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (rooftop concert to prove they are still together, things do not go as expected); Klaus lets Todd play bass while saying forgiveness is not owed yet, and the band trusts Holly's trust me; cliffhanger: Goldenshorts announces Holly in DMBEETZ

rows.synopsis: A shocking twist changes everything. In the aftermath, the Brushstrokes dig deep to support a friend.
rows.situation: going undercover to expose a lie; being cut off from your friends and lonely for them; trusting a friend when it looks like betrayal
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (a shocking twist changes everything, the band digs deep to support a friend); Holly reveals her plan to expose DMBEETZ as robots and the band welcomes her back; content consideration: parents cutting off a friendship, resolved with apology

rows.synopsis: As Ms. Goldenshorts deals with DMBEETZ drama, the Brushstrokes get trapped in Mr. Hitmaker's studio.
rows.situation: understanding why someone became hard (the rule-enforcer's sad backstory); being trapped and needing family; telling a parent the truth about the life you want
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (Ms Goldenshorts deals with DMBEETZ drama, the band is trapped in the studio); Holly's honest voicemail to her mom and the mom's too-tight apology carry the resolution; the journal shows Goldenshorts once wanted what the kids want and gave up; content consideration: mild peril, resolved

rows.synopsis: It's a race against time to stop Ms. Goldenshorts. Can the Brushstrokes pull off one more show and inspire fans to paint their own destinies?
rows.situation: a town about to give up all its choices out of fear; being seen for who you are and taken seriously anyway; an adult who forgot she once wanted to be free
rows.notes: script; identity verified vs synopsis (race to stop Ms Goldenshorts, one more show, inspiring fans to paint their own destinies); the town refuses conformity and the kids are revealed and believed; compassion for Goldenshorts, it is also not our fault that you just gave up; series ends with everyone free to choose
